newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat profits tumble, outlook cautious.
newsitem.headline: Fiat profits tumble, outlook cautious.

text.p: Italian industrial giant Fiat said Thursday its operating profits nearly halved in 1996, indicating tough conditions for its core car-making division, and painted a cautious outlook for this year.

Italy's largest private industrial group said its 1996 operating profits slid to around 1.8 trillion lire ($1.1 billion) from 1995's 3.325 trillion lire ($2.08 billion), while annual sales rose just 3 percent to around 78 trillion lire ($49 billion).

But in the group's traditional "letter to shareholders," Fiat reported that its 1996 pretax profit would rise slightly to around 3.5 trillion lire ($2.18 billion) from 3.4 trillion lire ($2.13 billion) in 1995 due to one-time gains made during the last quarter of 1996.

"In 1997 the group will find itself operating in a environment of very difficult markets. European markets will show modest growth, while the competition will continue to follow extremely aggressive commercial policies," Fiat chairman Cesare Romiti told the group's shareholders.
Romiti added in his first letter to shareholders since taking over as chairman from Gianni Agnelli in early 1996 that Fiat was committed to improving profitability.

The Italian government's incentive plan offering discounts to buyers who trade in cars more than 10 years old for new models was an important measure to help demand recover in a depressed market, he said.
